newsitem.title: FRANCE: Heir to France's Foccart tries to stop memoirs.
newsitem.headline: Heir to France's Foccart tries to stop memoirs.

text.p: The heir of Jacques Foccart has threatened to stop publication of the next instalment of the veteran French Africa policymaker's memoirs unless he can see the proofs first, the daily newspaper Le Monde said on Thursday.
It said Robert Rigaud, 76, had taken publishing house Fayard to court to demand the right to review the proofs of the second volume of "Foccart Speaks", which is due for release on April 9.
Henri Leclerc, a lawyer representing Fayard, said Rigaud had not produced any document to show that Foccart wanted the work be withdrawn.
Le Monde said Foccart postponed publishing the book when he resumed his role as presidential adviser on African policy after President Jacques Chirac was elected in 1995.
Other reports have said he deferred publication until after his death because the book contains explosive revelations.
The first volume, published in 1995, had left many gaps in his cloak-and-dagger career spanning a quarter of a century.
"He was a legendary personality who knew many African heads of state and many secrets," Rigaud's lawyer, Lucien Sberro, told Le Monde.
The second volume consists of a series of interviews by journalist Philippe Gaillard in which Foccart discusses his behind-the-scenes orchestration of French policy in Africa over 25 years.
Le Monde said Foccart yielded rights to the interviews to Gaillard's employer, the weekly magazine Jeune Afrique under a July, 1994, contract.
A member of the late President Charles de Gaulle's inner circle, Foccart had a reputation for using dubious and violent methods to maintain or overthrow African leaders according to Paris' interests.
